                  RESOLUTION C H A P T E R 252
     Assembly Concurrent Resolution No. 216—Relative to
                   brucellosis eradication.
                [Filed with Secretary of State July 24, 1969.]

    WHEBBAS, The California Dairy Animal Health Committee,
formerly the Statewide Bang's Disease Committee, has been
 organized and active since 1938; and
    WHEREAS, The committee, representing California's beef and
 dairy and swine industries in combating brucellosis, an infec-
 tious disease of man and animal which would cause losses ex-
ceeding $25 million annually if it remained unchecked, has
coordinated its efforts with the State Department of Agricul-
ture, University of California, and other governmental agen-
cies ; and
    WHEREAS, Its enlightened attitude led to the development of
recommendations and public relations resulting in a statewide
effort toward eradicating the disease; and
    WHEREAS, The 20-year campaign to eradicate bovine bru-
cellosis ended in success in May 1969; and
    WHEREAS, California now qualifies, after 10 years (1938-
1948) of pioneering efforts, for federal certification as a bo-
vine brucellosis-free state, with the official effort to eradicate
brucellosis starting with a calf vaccination program in 1948
and the testing of cattle program in 1957; and
   WHEREAS, Joe H a r t of Stanislaus County, the only original
producer member remaining on the committee, has served as
the one and only chairman of an active committee; now, there-
fore, be it
   Resolved by the Assembly of the State of California, the
Senate thereof concurring, That the members commend Joe
Hart and the many livestock producers who have served on
the California Dairy Animal Health Committee, the State De-
partment of Agriculture, University of California, other gov-
ernmental agencies and related industries; and be it further
   Resolved, That the Chief Clerk of the Assembly transmit a
suitably prepared copy of this resolution to Joe Hart, the
State Department of Agriculture, and the University of Cali-
fornia.

more such officers. The council shall prescribe the duties of all

vided in this Chapter.''

 30,1948; and

 authorized for financial participation by the California Legis-

 and private property, endangered lives, and created great
hardship for the residents of the basin; and

these floods could have been prevented had the authorized fea-
tures of the Santa Clara River Flood Control Project been con-
structed and in operation; and

additional project reports on the Santa Clara River Basin,
including a report currently being prepared for flood control

nia and of the United States; now, therefore, be it
   Resolved by the Senate and Assembly of the State of Cali-

Santa Clara River Flood Control Project; and be it further
   Resolved, That the United States Army Corps of Engineers

of necessary flood control works at the earliest possible time;

   Resolved, That the Secretary of the Senate transmit copies

               RESOLUTION CHAPTER 258
       Senate Concurrent Resolution No. 81—Relative to
          state water projects in Los Angeles County.
             [Filed with Secretary of State July 81, 1969.]

   WHEREAS, The State of California has undertaken the con-
struction of a State Water Resources Development System in
order to develop water supplies necessary to meet the growing
demands of its rapidly expanding population; and
   WHEREAS, The State Water Resources Development System
affords the opportunity to provide a wide variety of benefits,
including water supply, flood control, hydroelectric power gen-
eration, recreation, and fish and wildlife enhancement; and
   WHEREAS, The Legislature, in recognition of the vast op-
portunities this project presented to enhance the state's fish
and wildlife resources and to provide statewide recreation
benefits, enacted the Davis-Dolwig Act, declaring recreation
and fish and wildlife enhancement to be purposes of all state
water projects; and
   WHEREAS, Significant accomplishments have already been
realized as a result of this specific legislative policy declara-
tion ; and
   WHEREAS, The attainment of the goals sought by the Legis-
lature through the passage of the Davis-Dolwig Act has not
always been accomplished without difficulty, inasmuch as the
use of land and water for various beneficial purposes is not in
all instances compatible; and
   WHEREAS, Considerable difficulty has been encountered in
formulating an acceptable recreational development program
for the Castaic Reservoir, the Pyramid Reservoir, and portions
of the California Aqueduct located in Los Angeles County be-
cause of such competing uses of land and water; and
   WHEREAS, The Castaic Reservoir is a multiple-purpose facil-
ity designed to provide a multiplicity of benefits for the people
of California; and
   WHEREAS, The development of facilities to provide benefits
for specific project purposes consistent with the development
of facilities for all other beneficial purposes is dependent upon
the formulation of a comprehensive plan which sets forth gen-
eral guidelines for the total development of the project; and
   WHEREAS, The formulation of a comprehensive plan for the
Castaic Reservoir Complex will require the consideration of a
wide variety of interests and is necessary to assure the attain-
ment of the maximum possible benefit afforded by the project;
now, therefore, be it
                         1969
Res. Ch. 259]                   REGTTLAK SESSION                 3929

  Resolved by the Senate of the State of California, the As-
sembly thereof concurring, That the Department of Water Re-
sources, in cooperation with the Department of Parks and Rec-
reation and the Department of Fish and Game, are directed to
formulate a comprehensive plan for the Castaie Reservoir
Complex, the Pyramid Reservoir, and portions of the Cali-
fornia Aqueduct located in Los Angeles County, and to develop
the comprehensive plan for the Castaie Reservoir in full coop-
eration with the County of Los Angeles and the United States
Forest Service; and be it further
  Resolved, That the Secretary of the Senate transmit copies
of this resolution to the Director of Parks and Recreation,
the Director of Water Resources, and the Director of Fish and
Game.

                  RESOLUTION C H A P T E R 259
       Senate Concurrent Resolution No. 93—Relative to
              water pollution abatement practices.
                [Filed with Secretary of State July 31, 1969.]

   WHEREAS, The pollution of water presents an imminent
danger to the health of all citizens, and presents a grave threat
to the recreation, wildlife, and aesthetic potentials of water
use; and
   WHEKEAS, The pollution of water is contrary to the legal
doctrine of beneficial use for water rights allocation; and
   WHEREAS, The right to divert and use waters of the state
for domestic, industrial, or agricultural purposes does not
imply the right to discharge waste water of a quality lower
than that of the water diverted; and
   WHEREAS, Existing water pollution regulation has proved to
be inadequate to effectively control water quality in the public
interest; and
   WHEREAS, The pollution of water results in enormous public
expense for damage repair and pollution abatement caused by
the pollution by private water users; and
   WHEREAS, That the public is ultimately assessed for the cost
of pollution which is caused by private water users is un-
justifiable ; and
   WHEREAS, The precedent and example of the assessment of
fees on water users who discharge waste waters which utilize
the assimilative capacity of any waters within a given political
jurisdiction are provided by the Federal Republic of Germany
in the Ruhr Valley; now, therefore, be it
  Resolved by the Senate of the State of California, the As-
sembly thereof concurring, That the State Water Resources
Control Board is directed to conduct a contrastive study of
water pollution abatement practices as existing in the State
of California and in the Federal Republic of Germany; that
3930              STATUTES OF CALIFORNIA                  [ReS. Ch. 260

such study assess the German fee assessment practice, includ-
ing the amount of fee rates, the criteria for stream quality
upon which the rates are based, and the political and judicial
structures which administer the fee assessment; that such
study determine the technical applicability Of such fee assess-
ment practice to the water pollution situation in the State of
California; that such study determine the political feasibility
of establishing fee assessment practice, on water users who
pollute water, as public policy; and that such study determine
reasonable standards, criteria, and specifications upon which
a fee assessment practice could be applied for the unique needs
of the State of California; and be it further
   Resolved, That the State "Water Resources Control Board
shall report its findings and recommendations thereon, includ-
 ing its recommendations concerning any necessary legislation,
 to the Legislature not later than the 30th legislative day of
 the 1970 Regular Session of the Legislature; and be it
further
   Resolved, That the Secretary of the Senate transmit a copy
 of this resolution to the State Water Resources Control Board.


                RESOLUTION CHAPTER 260
       Senate Joint Resolution No. 18—Relating to mineral
          extraction from outer continental shelf lands.
             [Filed with Secretary of State July 31, 1969.]

   WHEREAS, The State of California has for many years been
engaged in the study of coastal marine resources, including
mineral resources, to determine the methods whereby such re-
sources may best be utilized and protected; and
   WHEREAS, The federal government exercises, by virtue of
its sovereignty, jurisdiction over outer continental shelf lands ;
and
   WHEREAS, The United States Department of the Interior has
entered into a mineral extraction leasing program with respect
to outer continental shelf lands adjacent to the coastal states;
and
   WHEREAS, This program will have a decided impact upon
the coastal environment of the states adjoining the outer con-
tinental shelf lands under lease, and the recent oil leakage
disaster off the California coast is tragic evidence of the terri-
ble impact such oil and gas operations may have upon the
marine and coastal resources of adjacent states; and
   WHEREAS, Congress is currently considering legislation af-
fecting the coastal resources of the various states adjoining
the outer continental shelf lands and the revenues derived
from such lands, which legislation would provide for the aug-
mentation of the Land and Water Conservation F u n d ; and
                    1969
Res. Ch. 260]              REGULAR SESSION                   3931

    WHEREAS, The State of California recognizes the need for
increased funding of the Land and Water Conservation Fund,
in order to permit the acquisition and development of land and
water resources by the various states pursuant to the Land and
Water Conservation F u n d Act of 1965 (Public Law 88-578;
78 Stat. 897); and
    WHEREAS, The disposition of the revenues derived from the
outer continental shelf lands should take into consideration the
impact which the mineral extraction leasing program will have
upon the coastal environment of the coastal states; now, there-
fore, be it
     Resolved by the Senate and Assembly of the State of Cali-
fornia, jointly, That the Legislature of the State of California
memorializes Congress to recognize the precedent established
in the so-called Mineral Lands Leasing Act of 1920 which al-
locates to the particular state involved 37£ percent of proceeds
derived from mineral extraction from federal lands located
 within such state; and to recognize, further, that the Land and
 Water Conservation F u n d should be augmented with addi-
 tional moneys (as determined by the Secretary of the Interior),
 provided that such funds are taken from money in the United
 States Treasury not otherwise allocated, together with funds
 specified under subsections (a), (b) and (c) of Section 2 of
 Title I of the Land and Water Conservation F u n d Act of 1965;
 and be it further
     Resolved, That the Legislature of the State of California
 fully supports any measure which affirms the concept of al-
 locating portions of the funds derived from mineral extraction
 to the states adjoining outer continental shelf lands for the pur-
 pose of serving the national interest; and be it further
     Resolved, That the Legislature of the State of California
 recognizes the need for Congress to provide subsidence and oil
 seepage disaster protection for the states located adjacent to
  the outer continental shelf lands; and be it further
     Resolved, That the Legislature of the State of California
 memorializes Congress to enact legislation creating a commis-
  sion composed of both federal and state technical personnel to
  establish drilling and safety practices for the development of
  the oil resources of the outer continental shelf; and be it
  further
      Resolved, That the Secretary of the Senate transmit copies
  of this resolution to the President and Vice President of the
  United States, to the Speaker of the House of Representatives,
   to the Secretary of the Interior, and to each Senator and Rep-
  resentative from California in the Congress of the United
 States.

amended as follows :
  First—That Article X I I is repealed.
  Second—That Article X I I is added, to read :

                         ARTICLE X I I
                         PUBLIC UTILITIES

   SEC. 1. The Public Utilities Commission consists of 5 mem-
bers, or more if prescribed by statute, appointed by the Gov-
ernor and approved by the Senate, a majority of the member-
ship concurring, for staggered 6-year terms. A vacancy is filled
for the remainder of the term. The Legislature may remove a
member for incompetence, neglect of duty, or corruption, two
thirds of the membership of each house concurring.
   SEC. 2. Private corporations and persons that own, oper-
ate, control, or manage a line, plant or system for the trans-
portation of people or property, the transmission of messages,
or the furnishing of heat, light, water, power, storage or wharf-
                     196
fees. Ch. 264]             9 REGULAR SESSION                 3935

age, directly or indirectly to or for the public, and common
carriers, are public utilities subject to control by the Legisla-
ture. The Legislature may prescribe that additional classes of
private corporations or persons are public utilities.
   SEC. 3. The Commission shall have such jurisdiction and
such legislative, executive, and judicial powers as are conferred
upon it by the Legislature, which are cognate and germane
to the regulation of public utilities. The manner and scope of
review of Commission action in a court of record shall be pro-
vided by statute.
   A city, county, or other public body may not regulate mat-
ters over which the Legislature grants regulatory power to
the Commission. This section does not affect power over public
utilities relating to the making and enforcement of police,
sanitary, and other regulations concerning municipal affairs
pursuant to a city charter existing on October 10, 1911, unless
that power has been revoked by the city's electors, or the right
of any city to grant franchises for public utilities or other
businesses on terms, conditions, and in the manner prescribed
by law.
   SEC. 4. The Legislature may provide that on request of
condemnor and condemnee the Commission fix just compensa-
tion for public utility property taken by eminent domain.

                   RESOLUTION C H A P T E R 265
  Senate Joint Resolution No. 28—Relative to oil pollution.
                [Filed with Secretary of State August 1, 1969.]

   WHEREAS, I t is the desire of the people of California to
protect the ocean waters, coastline, and marine resources of
this state from pollution by oil; and
   WHEREAS, One major source of pollution to the coastal
environment is caused by oil washing ashore from tankers that
surreptitiously clean their tanks near our shores; and
   WHEREAS, This oil causes great harm to the marine and
coastal biology and wildlife resources, despoils beaches and
coastline, impairs valuable recreational uses, costs taxpayers
thousands of dollars to remove, and results in considerable
economic loss to shoreline communities; and
   WHEREAS, The United States is a contracting nation to
the International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution
of the Seas by Oil, thereby establishing a zone extending 50
miles off our coast in which registered vessels of all contracting
nations are prohibited from discharging oil; and
   WHEREAS, If such an oil discharge takes place outside of
the territorial waters of the United States, although within the
protective zone, the United States does not have authority
under the treaty to punish any vessel of any contracting nation
other than its own; and
   WHEREAS, Oil imports have risen over 100 million tons in
the past 20 years and American flag vessels carry only 5
percent of the oil imports into the United States; and
   WHEREAS, The United States tanker fleet is governed by
substantially adequate domestic laws and most American ves-
sels are operating under a voluntary "clean seas" policy which
prohibits the discharge of persistent oils into any part of any
ocean; and
   WHEREAS, A S long as foreign vessels are preeminent in
the oil import trade, the domestic law of the United States is
 inadequate to deal with the discharge of oil in connection with
tanker operations and protection must be sought through
international channels; and
   WHEREAS, The United States has set the international com-
munity a good example with respect to the control of oil
 discharges from tankers and demonstrated a need for a world-
 wide "clean seas" policy; now, therefore, be it
   Resolved hy the Senate and Assembly of the State of Cali-
fornia, jointly, That the Legislature of the State of California
3938               STATUTES OF CALIFORNIA                [ReS. Ch. 266

respectfully memorializes the President and the Congress of
the United States to take immediate steps to commence nego-
tiations with other countries toward the formulation of inter-
national conventions to extend controls over the discharge of
oil and other hazardous substances into international waters
beyond the zones presently proscribed, to establish interna-
tional policies for "clean w a t e r s " on the high seas, and to
provide adequate deterrent to violators; and be it further
   Resolved, That the Secretary of the Senate transmit copies
of this resolution to the President and Vice President of the
United States, to the Speaker of the House of Representatives,
and to each Senator and Representative from California in the
Congress of the United States.


               RESOLUTION CHAPTER 266
Senate Concurrent Resolution No. 95—Relative to a study of
      the property tax exemption for homes for the aged.
            [Filed with Secretary of State August 2, 1969.]

   WHEREAS, Homes for the needy aged were granted property
tax exemption under the constitutional provision allowing
relief to religious, hospital, and charitable organizations; and
   WHEREAS, Homes for the needy aged relieve government of
a responsibility to provide care and expensive housing facili-
ties for certain persons who cannot care for themselves; and
   WHEREAS, The contended exemption also has been extended
to retirement homes and apartments which are not designed to
serve the needy; and
   WHEREAS, Persons of means living in such facilities can
escape local property taxes while less affluent senior citizens
living in their own homes must continue to pay property
taxes; and
   WHEREAS, The number of these new retirement homes is
increasing rapidly, mainly in urban centers and in a number
of smaller communities; and
   WHEREAS, These new retirement facilities have removed $58
million of assessed value from the tax rolls of local govern-
ments while adding additional service needs for these local
governments; now, therefore, be it
   Resolved by the Senate of the State of California, the As-
sembly thereof concurring, That the Joint Legislative Budget
Committee is hereby requested to review the law under which
this exemption is now granted to all homes for the aged re-
gardless of whether they serve needy or affluent members;
and be it further
   Resolved, That the Joint Legislative Budget Committee shall
examine:
   (1) Which portion of the cost of these homes is devoted to
welfare-type activities as distinct from residential care; and
                     1969
Res. Ch. 267]               JUGULAR SESSION                   3939

   (2) What are the equity considerations in granting prop-
erty tax exemptions for the residential portion of these facili-
ties; and be it further
   Resolved, That the Joint Legislative Budget Committee is
directed to report its findings and recommendations to the
Legislature by the 30th calendar day of the 1970 Regular
Session of the Legislature; and be it further
   Resolved, That this study shall not be interpreted or used
in any way to forestall cities from imposing a business license
tax or any other tax on life-care homes which are exempt
from property taxation.

                RESOLUTION CHAPTER 267
Senate Concurrent Resolution No. 123—Relative to Senate
  Bill No. 2 of the 1969 Regular Session of the Legislature.
            [Filed with Secretary of State August 2, 1969.]

   "WHEREAS, At its 1969 Regular Session, the Legislature
enacted Senate Bill No. 2 as Chapter 24 of the Statutes to
provide for financing the completion of the rapid transit
system of the San Francisco Bay Area Rapid Transit District
in the principal amount of $150,000,000, plus various costs
and interest payments, by means of a district transactions and
use tax at the rate of one-half of 1 percent; and
   WHEREAS, I n enacting Senate Bill No. 2, it is the intent of
the Legislature that the taxpayers in the San Francisco Bay
Area Rapid Transit District shall be required to pay no more
than the actual amount necessary to finance the completion
of the rapid transit system; and
   WHEREAS, The Legislature so provided for the protection of
the taxpayers in Senate Bill No. 2, wherein it adds Section
29140.5 to the Public Utilities Code to provide that, "if other
methods of financing shall hereafter be approved as a result
of other legislation hereafter enacted, then to the extent of
any funds received by the district under such other method
of financing, after deducting expenses of collection, the amount
of revenues from transactions and use taxes pursuant to this
article authorized under Section 29142 shall be reduced in
order that such taxes shall earlier terminate''; and
   WHEREAS, The purpose of the above provision is to protect
the taxpayers in the San Francisco Bay Area Rapid Transit
District by providing for a termination of the district's trans-
actions and use tax at the earliest possible date, and it is
immaterial whether legislation hereafter enacted is by the
Legislature of the State of California or the Congress of the
United States, so long as other methods of financing are made
available to the district to complete its transit system, if such
financing may be used for the purposes of reducing the prin-
cipal amount of $150,000,000 and is not earmarked for some
3940              STATUTES OF CALIFORNIA                 [Res. Ch. 268

specified purpose, such as the acquisition of rolling stock; now,
therefore, be it
   Resolved by the Senate of the State of California, the As-
sembly thereof concurring, That the Legislature, by adding
Section 29140.5 to the Public Utilities Code at its 1969 Regular
Session, intends that such section shall apply to both state and
federal legislation hereafter enacted, unless such legislation
earmarks the grant for specified purposes; and be it further
   Resolved, That the Secretary of the Senate transmit a copy
of this resolution to the Board of Directors of the San Fran-
cisco Bay Area Rapid Transit District.

per year; and
   WHEREAS, PAL today fields over 70 baseball teams, 41 soccer

erates programs in track and field, boxing, judo, and swim-
ming, reflecting PAL's greater and greater emphasis upon
summer activities so that during this traditionally idle time
youngsters can participate in healthful sporting activities pro-
viding at the same time recreation and experience in sports-
manship and fair play; and
   WHEREAS, The newly formed law enforcement division pro-
vides high school age students an inside view of law enforce-
ment with instruction in all phases of police work, including
investigations, patrol work, and trials, and includes tours of
various state law enforcement agencies and many kinds of
on-the-scene instruction; and
                      1969
Ees. Ch. 269]                REGULAB SESSION                  3941
   "WHEREAS, The PAL program represents a significant and
highly commendable effort to provide thousands of youngsters
an opportunity not otherwise available to participate in or-
ganized sporting events, and is a positive and constructive
approach to the problems of juvenile delinquency through its
involvement with the young; now, therefore, be it
   Resolved by the Senate of the State of California, the As-
sembly thereof concurring, That the members congratulate the
San Franciso Police Athletic League on the occasion of its
10th anniversary, and commend the organization for its in-
terest in and positive programs on behalf of the city's youth;
and be it further

                RESOLUTION C H A P T E E 269
      Senate Concurrent Resolution No. 149—Relative to
               memorializing Russell E. Pettit.
            [Filed with Secretary of State August 2, 1969.]

   WHEREAS, The Members of the Legislature of the State of
California were saddened to learn of the death of Russell E.
Pettit, prominent San Jose civic leader and dean of the na-
tion's chamber of commerce officials; and
   WHEREAS, Born in Maywood, Illinois, Mr. Pettit received
his education at the University of Chicago where he received
a bachelor of philosophy degree, and after traveling in Europe
and working for advertising firms in Chicago and San Fran-
cisco he came to San Jose; and
   WHEREAS, In 1925, Mr. Pettit became manager of publicity
and conventions of the Greater San Jose Chamber of Com-
merce; from 1928 to 1932, he was manager of the San Jose
Fiesta de las Rosas Association; in 1930, he founded the San
Jose Junior Chamber of Commerce; and in 1936, he was
named general manager of the San Jose Chamber of Com-
merce, a post he held until his retirement on June 1, 1967; and
   WHEREAS, During his 42 years with the chamber, Mr. Pettit
played a key role in San Jose's growth from an agricultural
community to an industrial center and was the driving force
behind San Jose's industrial development program during and
immediately after World War I I ; and
   WHEREAS, Mr. Pettit was a leader in the formation of the
Santa Clara County Fair Association and served as secretary-
manager and a member of its board of directors; and
   WHEREAS, He was named one of the first San Jose Junior
Chamber of Commerce's Young Men of the Year, and was
3942               STATUTES OF CALIFORNIA                 [Ees. Ch. 270

honored by more than 700 persons at a testimonial banquet
in the County Fairgrounds Pavilion huilding on the occasion
of his retirement two years ago; and
  WHEREAS, This veteran civic leader was a past president
and director of the San Jose Rotary Club, past president of
the American Chamber of Commerce Executives and a member
of the San Jose State College Advisory Board and the San
Jose Concert Series Advisory Board; and
  WHEREAS, His other affiliations included the Masons, San
Jose Lodge No. 10; Shrine-Islam Temple, San Francisco; San
Jose Country Club; Press and Union League Club of San
Francisco, and the Commonwealth Club of California; and
   WHEREAS, Mr. Pettit was also active with the Santa Clara
County Council of Boy Scouts from 1931 to 1944 and from
1960 to 1963 was chairman of the special guests committee for
the annual "Scout-O-Eama"; and
   WHEREAS, The loss of this capable and public-spirited citi-
zen, who gave so generously of his time and energies for the
betterment of his community, will be deeply felt by his family,
his many close friends and the people of his community; now,
therefore, be it
   Resolved by the Senate of the State of California, the As-
sembly thereof concurring, That the members pay homage to
the memory of Russell B. Pettit and express their sorrow over
the loss of the dean of the nation's chamber of commerce
officials and a dedicated civic leader; and be it further
   Resolved, That the Secretary of the Senate transmit suitably
prepared copies of this resolution to his widow, Mrs. Eleanor
Pettit, his daughter, Mrs. Patricia L. Prickett, and his brother,
Dr. Richard D. Pettit.

                  RESOLUTION CHAPTER 271
Senate Joint Resolution No. 26—Relative to Sherman                Institute.
                [Piled with Secretary of State August 5, 1969.]

   WHEREAS, The Legislature is concerned with the educational
opportunities of California students; and
   WHEREAS, California Indians, as well as Indians of other
states, are students at Sherman Institute, a Bureau of Indian
Affairs boarding school, in Riverside, California; and
   WHEREAS, Indian students require, desire and are entitled
to educational opportunities on a parity with other students
throughout the State of California; and
   WHEREAS, Equal educational opportunities, equal educa-
tional facilities, curriculum, personnel, services, and direction
must be obtained; and
   WHEREAS, The physical plant, curriculum, and faculty
training of Sherman Institute do not meet the minimum
standards required in California for accreditation; and
   WHEREAS, Sherman Institute's library is outdated and in-
adequate as a reference library in that it is deficient in both
number and quality of recommended books and other resource
material necessary to meet the students' educational needs;
and
3944               STATUTES OF CALIFORNIA                  [ R e S - c h . 272

   "WHEREAS, There is insufficient personnel at Sherman Insti-
tute to provide the students with an equal educational oppor-
tunity in the areas of instruction, counseling, coaching, and
extracurricular activities at the school; and
   WHEREAS, Funds for clothing and travel for needy Indian
students are not available at Sherman Institute, although
funds are provided for this purpose at other federal Indian
schools; and
   WHEREAS, The most effective schools are those which are
governed by school boards that reflect the attitudes of the stu-
dents' parents; now, therefore, be it
   Resolved by the Senate and Assembly of the State of Cali-
fornia, jointly, That the Legislature of the State of California
respectfully memorializes the President and the Congress of the
United States to provide for an emergency appropriation to
Sherman Institute to enable the school to bring its physical
plant up to standards necessary for accreditation, to improve
the school's library system, to obtain adequate personnel, and
to provide adequate services and to budget funds on a con-
tinuing basis to insure Sherman Institute's ability to maintain
its facilities, curriculum, personnel and services at a level nec-
essary to meet the Indian students' educational needs and to
establish an all-Indian school board to direct the school's pro-
gram; and be it further
   Resolved, That the Secretary of the Senate transmit copies
of this resolution to the President and Vice President of the
United States, to the Speaker of the House of Representatives,
to each Senator and Representative from California in the
Congress of the United States, to the chairmen of the commit-
tees of the United States Congress dealing with the subject of
this resolution, to the Secretary of the Interior and to the
Commissioner of Indian Affairs.

    Assembly Joint Resolution No. 40—Relative to taxation
             of state and local government bonds.
             [Filed with Secretary of State August 7, 1969.]

  WHEREAS, Equity among taxpayers is essential to popular
confidence in the federal revenue system; and
  WHEREAS, The Ways and Means Committee of the United
States House of Representatives has conducted extensive hear-
ing on proposals for equitable reform of the federal personal
income t a x ; and
  WHEREAS, Spokesmen for the National Governors' Confer-
ence, the National Legislative Conference, The National Asso-
ciation of Attorneys General and the National Association of
State Treasurers, Auditors and Comptrollers have endorsed
Res. Ch. 273]            1969
                                REGULAR SESSION                   3945

the objective of tax reform while urging the committee to
refrain from changes which would weaken the capacity of
the states to meet the needs for state services; and
   WHEREAS, The Ways and Means Committee is to be com-
mended for its efforts to improve the equity of the federal
personal income t a x ; now, therefore, be it
   Resolved by the Assembly and Senate of the State of Cali-
fornia, jointly, That the Legislature of the State of California
respectfully memorializes the President and the Congress of
the United States:
   1. That no change be made which would deprive state and
local government obligations of their traditional immunity
from federal taxation;
   2. That no change be made which would result in constric-

governments;
   3. That no change be made which would interpose federal

governments; and

ties of the appropriation processes of the Congress; and be it

sentatives, and to each Senator and Representative from Cali-
fornia in the Congress of the United States.

                RESOLUTION C H A P T E R 275
      Senate Concurrent Resolution No. 153—Relative to
               memorializing LeRoy V. Brant.
            [Filed with Secretary of State August 7, 1969.]

   WHEREAS, The Members of the Legislature have learned with
sorrow of the death of LeRoy V. Brant, founder of the San
Jose Municipal Chorus and for many years the foremost musi-
cal figure of his community; and
   WHEREAS, Mr. Brant, the great-great-grandson of Mohawk
Chief Joseph Brant, head of the Six Nations during Revolu-
tionary War times, came from his native Nebraska to Cali-
fornia at the age of 17; and
   WHEREAS, In the 61 years which followed, he devoted his
life to music and to community activities which ranged from
volunteer service with the police auxiliary to politics; and
   WHEREAS, After graduation from Petaluma High School,
and from College of the Pacific with a bachelor of music de-
gree, he organized the first full music course in California
schools in Fort Bragg Union High School; and
   WHEREAS, In 1917, he came to San Jose and went on to be-
come an integral part of the city's musical life, founding the
San Jose Municipal Chorus in 1924 and conducting it until
his retirement in 1963; he also founded the Institute of Music,
the only privately owned, fully accredited academy of music
in Santa Clara County, and was its director until the time of
his death; and
394&               STATUTES OF CALIFORNIA                  [Res. Ch. 276

  "WHEREAS, Mr. Brant was a composer of countless sonatas, a
contributor to numerous national music publications, the orga-
nizer of the concert series for the San Jose Chapter of the
American Guild of Organists, the holder of five earned music
degrees, and, at various times, was music critic of the San Jose
Mercury-Herald and the San Jose Evening News; and
  WHEREAS, A 33rd degree Mason, inspector general honorary,
Mr. Brant was decorated knight commander of the Court of
Honor, Scottish Eite of Freemasonry, and he was organist for
the San Jose Scottish Eite Bodies for 35 years, retiring in
1954; and
  WHEREAS, He also was organist and choirmaster at Trinity
Episcopal Church for 24 years, retiring in 1946; he supervised
installation of the church organ and was designer of organs
for both the San Jose Scottish Rite Temple and the San Jose
Civic Auditorium; and he was also a member of the Santa
Clara County Music Teachers Association and the Santa Clara
County Republican Central Committee; now, therefore, be it
  Resolved by the Senate of the State of California, the As-
sembly thereof concurring, That the members express their
sincere condolences on the passing of LeRoy V. Brant to his
wife, Ruth; and be it further
   Resolved, That the Secretary of the Senate transmit a suit-
ably prepared copy of this resolution to Mrs. LeRoy V. Brant.

of the advertising in the above mentioned official paper of the
proposed charter amendment aforesaid.
   That at said general municipal election a majority of the
qualified electors voting upon said proposed charter amend-
ment voted in favor of it and adopted and ratified the same.
   That said amendment to the Charter of the City of San
Jose, so adopted and ratified by the qualified electors of said
City, amends said Charter as follows:

            CHARTER AMENDMENT—PROPOSITION           A

   That Section 1106 of the Charter of the City of San Jose
be amended to read as follows:
   "Section 1106. Employees of Consolidated Cities. Except
as otherwise required by such laws of the State of California
as are applicable to charter cities, all officers and employees of
any city (hereinafter called "consolidated city") hereafter
consolidated with the City of San Jose, who were full-time
officers or employees of such consolidated city upon the date
of election held in such consolidated city for such consolida-
tion, when such officers or employees would be included in the
classified service of the City of San Jose, shall from the ef-
fective date of such consolidation be deemed to have their
names upon eligible lists for respective types of positions held
by them, and to be qualified for appointment to such respec-
tive positions."

   We further certify that we have compared the text of the
foregoing amendment with the original proposal submitting
the same to the electors of said City and find that the fore-
going is a full, true, correct, complete and exact copy thereof.
That as to said amendment, this certificate shall be taken as a
full certification of the regularity of all proceedings had and
done in connection therewith.
   In witness whereof, we have hereunto set our hands and
have caused the corporate seal of the City of San Jose to be
affixed hereto this 10th day of July, 1969.

   WHEEEAS, Rehabilitation workshops for the handicapped are

3954                STATUTES OF CALIFORNIA                [Res. Ch. 281

of goods and services, many of which may be furnished

   Resolved by the Assembly of the State of California, the

the State of California helps insure, along with private in-

   Resolved by the Assembly of the State of California, the

   Resolved, That the members find and declare that the Fifth

               EESOLUTION CHAPTER 286
Assembly Joint Resolution No. 48—Relative to uniform            nation-
             wide standards of public assistance.
            [Filed with Secretary of State August 8, 1969.]

   WHEEEAS, It has long been the policy of the state and coun-
ties of California to provide public assistance for needy citi-
zens on a more adequate level than most states; and
   WHEREAS, The Legislature finds that the absence of uni-
form and equitable standards of aid to the needy among the
several states is a factor contributing significantly to the rising
number of public assistance recipients in California who have
recently migrated from other states; and
   WHEREAS, Recent changes in federal welfare laws and regu-
lations have shifted a greater financial burden to the state and
counties of California and thus reduced the federal share of
welfare costs; and
   WHEREAS, Recent court decisions and increased caseload
growth have combined to greatly increase state and county
welfare costs so that the situation is approaching crisis pro-
portions; now, therefore, be it
   Resolved by the Assembly and Senate of the State of Cali-
fornia, jointly, That the Legislature of the State of California
respectfully memorializes the President and Congress of the
United States to establish uniform and equitable standards of
aid on a nationwide basis in order to permit needy persons
to be more adequately aided in their native states and thus
reduce the impetus to migration because of unmet need; and
be it further
   Resolved, That pending the establishment of equitable stand-
ards of aid on a nationwide basis, the federal government
finance public assistance payments made to recipients who do
not meet the length of residence requirements that were oper-
ative in California and other states before being declared void
by federal courts, and that such federal financing continue in
each case until the length of residency requirements that were
in existence have been met by each recipient; and be it further
   Resolved, That the apparent policy of the federal govern-
ment to shift an ever greater proportion of the cost of welfare
to the states be reversed in view of the greater elasticity of
federal tax bases and resources over those available to state
and local governments; and be it further
   Resolved, That the Chief Clerk of the Assembly transmit
copies of this resolution to the President and Vice President
of the United States, to the Speaker of the House of Repre-
sentatives, and to each Senator and Representative from Cali-
fornia in the Congress of the United States.
                         1969
Ees. Ch. 288]                   REGULAR SESSION                   3959

         Assembly Joint Resolution No. 52—Relative to
               the California Maritime Academy.
                [Filed with Secretary of State August 8, 1969.]

   WHEREAS, The California Maritime Academy has been estab-

since 1959-60; and
   WHEREAS, The decreased percent of federal funding is due to

normal price and program cost increases; now, therefore, be it
   Resolved by the Assembly and Senate of the State of
California, jointly, That the Legislature of the State of Califor-

of the United States to increase the federal government's share
of funding for the California Maritime Academy to its pre-
vious level; and be it further
   Resolved, That the Chief Clerk of the Assembly transmit
copies of this resolution to the President and Vice President of
the United States, to the Speaker of the House of Represent-
atives, to each Senator and Representative from California in
the Congress of the United States, and the Board of Governors
of the California Maritime Academy.


                   EESOLUTION CHAPTER 288
          Assembly Joint Resolution No. 59—Relative
             to federal-aid primary highway funds.
                [Filed with Secretary of State August 8, 1969.]

   WHEREAS, The federal-aid primary highway system in Cali-
fornia includes some of the nation's best known routes, such
as Route 101 on the California coast, Route 50 from Sacra-
mento to Lake Tahoe, and Route 1, the Pacific Coast Highway,
from Ventura to San Clemente; and
   WHEREAS, The geographical expanse of California lends
itself to use of the motor vehicle as the primary means of
meeting the transportation needs of the people of this state;
and
3960                STATUTES OF CALIFORNIA                    [ R e s . Ch. 289

    WHEREAS, The Eedwood National Park and Point Reyes
 National Park have recently been established within the state
 and these parks will generate additional traffic on federal-aid
 primary system as well as our state highways in areas of the
 state where such systems are already seriously inadequate to
 service present traffic demands; and
    WHEREAS, The improvement of a large portion of the mile-
 age on this system which is needed now cannot be budgeted
 because of the lack of funds; and
    WHEREAS, Federal gasoline taxes collected are approxi-
 mately 20 percent greater than the road funds returned to
 California from the federal government; and
    WHEREAS, Substantial deficiencies in federal, state and local
 highways and roads in California would seem to indicate a
 greater portion of federal funds should be returned to Cali-
 fornia to help meet its highway needs; and
    WHEREAS, The method for distributing federal funds to the
 states for use on the primary system was first developed in
 1916 and is based upon one-third population, one-third area,
 and one-third post road mileage; and
    WHEREAS, The California Department of Public Works is
 now undertaking a federally mandated functional classification
 study of all streets and highways in the state; and
    WHEREAS, Such functional classification study may substan-
 tially affect the distribution of federal funds throughout the
 state; and
    WHEREAS, Additional factors, such as miles of roadway,
number of fatal and injury accidents, vehicle miles traveled,
and motor vehicle registrations should be considered in dis-
tributing funds; now, therefore, be it
    Besolved by the Assembly and Senate of the State of Cali-
fornia, jointly, That the Legislature of the State of California
respectfully memorializes the President and the Congress of
the United States to enact legislation to provide for the dis-
tribution of federal-aid primary highway funds on a more
currently realistic basis than the outdated formula now used;
and be it further
   Besolved, That the Chief Clerk of the Assembly transmit
copies of this resolution to the President and Vice President
of the United States, the Secretary of the Department of
Transportation, the Speaker of the House of Representatives,
and to each Senator and Representative from California in
the Congress of the United States.


               RESOLUTION CHAPTER 289
Assembly Joint Besolution No. 47—Belative to the federal
  food-stamp and commodity distribution programs in Cali-
  fornia.
            [Filed with Secretary ol State August 8, 1969.]
                      1969
Res. Ch. 290]                REGULAR SESSION                  3961

   WHEREAS, The Congress has created food-stamp and com-
modity distribution programs, which have been implemented
by legislative action in California; and
   WHEREAS, These programs were designed by Congress to
provide surplus food to the hungry and needy " t o the maxi-
mum extent practicable''; and
   WHEREAS, On December 30, 1968, a federal court in San
Francisco ordered the United States Secretary of Agriculture
to immediately implement one or both of these food supple-
ment programs in every California county, but thus far the
secretary has taken no action to implement the programs in
counties of California which presently do not operate them;
and
   WHEREAS, The federal court also found that there is sub-
stantial hunger in each California county without a food sup-
plement program, and that sufficient federal funds are avail-
able to implement the programs; now, therefore, be it
   Resolved by the Assembly and Senate of the State of Cali-
fornia, jointly, That the Legislature of the State of California
respectfully requests the President and Congress of the United
States to transfer the administration of the federal food-
stamp and commodity distribution programs from the United
States Department of Agriculture to the United States De-
partment of Health, Education, and Welfare, where their
implementation may receive a more favorable response; and
be it further
   Resolved, That the President and the Congress of the United
States are urged to investigate the reluctance of the United
States Department of Agriculture to implement these pro-
grams in California pursuant to federal court order to deter-
mine if congressional intent has not been observed; and be it
further
   Resolved, That the Chief Clerk of the Assembly transmit
copies of this resolution to the President and Vice President
of the United States, to the Speaker of the House of Repre-
sentatives, to the Secretary of Agriculture, to the Secretary of
Health, Education, and Welfare, and to each Senator and
Representative from California in the Congress of the United
States.

                RESOLUTION C H A P T E R 290
Senate Concurrent Resolution No. 14—Relative to the creation
  of the Joint Committee on Reorganization of Large Urban
  School Districts.
            [Piled with Secretary of State August 8, 1969.]

  Resolved by the Senate of the State of California, the As-
sembly thereof concurring, As follows:
  1. The Joint Committee on Reorganization of Large Urban
Unified School Districts is hereby created and authorized and
3962               STATUTES OF CALIFORNIA           [Res. Ch. 290

directed to ascertain, study and analyze all facts relating to the
Los Angeles City School District and the advisability, from
a governmental and educational standpoint, of dividing the
 district into smaller units or of any other suitable solution,
 including an analysis of the most practical methods and forms
of reorganization which would accomplish such a solution. The
committee shall also ascertain, study and analyze the whole
need of the Los Angeles City School District and the complex
problems facing the district as a result of the concentration
of minority groups, the heavy centralization of poverty in the
core area of the city, and the large size of the district. The
committee shall also study and analyze, including, but not
limited to, the operation, effect, administration, enforcement
and needed revision of any and all laws in any way bearing
upon or relating to the subject of this resolution, and to report
thereon to the Legislature, including in the report its recom-
mendations for appropriate legislation.
    2. The committee shall consist of five Members of the Senate,
 appointed by the Committee on Rules thereof, and five Mem-
bers of the Assembly, appointed by the Speaker thereof. Va-
cancies occurring in the membership of the committee shall be
filled by the appointing power.
    3. The committee is authorized to act during this session of
the Legislature, including any recess, and after final adjourn-
ment until the commencement of the 1970 Regular Session,
with authority to file its final report not later than June 30,
1970.
   4. The committee and each subcommittee thereof is author-
ized to leave the State of California in the performance of its
duties.
   5. The committee and its members shall have and exercise
all of the rights, duties and powers conferred upon investigat-
ing committees and their members by the provisions of the
Joint Rules of the Senate and Assembly as they are adopted
and amended from time to time at this session, which provisions
are incorporated herein and made applicable to this committee
and its members.
   6. The committee has the following additional powers and
duties:
    (a) To select a chairman and a vice chairman from its mem-

                RESOLUTION CHAPTER 292
 Senate Concurrent Resolution No. 72—Relative to urging the
   Department of Mental Hygiene to apply the methods of the
   Geriatric Screening Project of San Francisco.
             [Filed with Secretary of State August 8, 1969.]

    WHEREAS, Because of the spectacular results of the Geriatric
  Screening Project, initiated and funded by the 1963 Legisla-
  ture, the City and. County of San Francisco have made the
 project a permanent part of their program; and
    WHEREAS, The high rate of "inappropriate commitments"
  among our aged population has for many years harmed those
 so committed, overburdened the state facilities, and reduced
 the care available to those most in need; and
    WHEREAS, The small staff of highly trained persons from the
 Department of Mental Hygiene, working in cooperation with
 San Francisco Community Health Services, placed the empha-
 sis on screening patients in their home surroundings prior to
 admission to county facilities; and
    WHEREAS, Their efforts resulted in a drop in county admis-
 sions from 661 to 262 per year by 1967, and a staggering cut
 in state commitments from 306 in 1964 to 3 in 1967; and
    WHEREAS, Out of a total of 1,290 persons screened during
 1965, 1966, and 1967, the team found it possible to continue
 the care of 45 percent of these people in the security and com-
 fort of their own homes by the use of some supportive services;
 and
    WHEREAS, Out of the entire number screened during this
 period, 51 percent were placed in nursing homes, boarding
 homes, county and private medical hospitals, leaving an almost
 unbelievable 4 percent for commitment to state hospitals; and
    WHEREAS, The project was honored in 1966 by the APA
 Hospital and Community Psychiatry Service Achievement
 Award; and
    WHEREAS, The wide application of methods developed by this
project will result in great benefits to the individual geriatric
patients and will mean better and more concentrated care for
a smaller number of patients in state institutions, with sub-
stantial savings to the state; now, therefore, be it
   Resolved hy the Senate of the State of California, the Assem-
bly thereof concurring, That the Department of Mental Hy-
giene be urged to institute a statewide county-by-county pro-
gram to persuade the several counties to adopt methods
developed by the geriatric team; and be it further
   Resolved, That the department be requested to submit a pro-
gram report to the Legislature by the 30th day of the 1970
session; and be it further
   Resolved, That the Secretary of the Senate transmit copies
of this resolution to the Department of Mental Hygiene and
to the board of supervisors of each county.

Senate Concurrent Resolution No. 87—Relating to the estab-

  fornia.
                 [Filed with Secretary of State August 8, 1969.]

   WHEREAS, The 1965 Legislature adopted Assembly Concur-
rent Resolution No. 85 (Stats. 1965, Res. Ch. 151), calling
upon the Board of Regents of the University of California to
conduct an in-depth study of the feasibility and advisability
of establishing a second school of veterinary medicine to be
located in southern California in the near future; and
   WHEREAS, The regents thereafter instructed its staff to con-
duct such a study, and a report was rendered by a special
academic committee appointed by the president of the univer-
sity in May of 1966, but has not yet been made public; and
   WHEREAS, That report asserted that the establishment of
such a school in the southern part of the state was feasible and
would fulfill the pressing need for training an increased num-
ber of doctors of veterinary medicine in southern California;
and
   WHEREAS, This report has been held in confidence by univer-
sity officials because of their concern that initiation of a
school of veterinary medicine in southern California at this
time would interfere with the orderly development of other
university medical schools, but there is no evidence to support
this fear nor is there any justifiable connection or overlap
between the two types of institutions; and
   WHEREAS, The 1968 Legislature adopted Senate Concurrent
Resolution No. 66 (Stats. 1968, Res. Ch. 187) urging the
Board of Regents of the University of California to make
public this special report and to accelerate planning and
budgeting for a southern school of veterinary medicine;
now, therefore, be it
   Resolved by the Senate of the State of California, the
Assembly thereof concurring, That the Board of Regents of
the University of California is urged to make public the
special report prepared in response to ACR 85 of the 1965
Regular Session of the Legislature; and be it further
   Resolved, That the Legislature strongly urges the board of
regents to accelerate planning and budgeting for a southern
California school of veterinary medicine, and to include
initial funds therefor in its 1970-71 budget proposals which
will be submitted to the Governor late this year; and be it
further
   Resolved, That the Secretary of the Senate transmit a copy
of this resolution to each member of the Board of Regents
of the University of California.

               KESOLUTION C H A P T E E 294
Senate Concurrent Resolution No. 119—Relative to the Miller-
             Unruh Basic Reading Act of 1965.
            [Filed with Secretary of State August 8, 1969.]

   WHEEEAS, Sixteen million dollars ($16,000,000) was appro-
priated for the Miller-Unruh Basic Reading Act of 1965 for
the 1968-1969 fiscal year; and
   WHEREAS, The inability of applicant school districts to em-
ploy the total number of specialist teachers in reading ap-
proved for funding by the Department of Education has
resulted in the allocation of less than the full appropriation;
 and
   WHEEEAS, Sufficient funds remain to provide for the em-
ployment on an annual basis of 77 additional specialist
teachers in reading; and
   WHEREAS, Other school districts would have become eligible
for funds for specialist teachers in reading had the inability
of approved applicant districts to employ the approved num-
ber of teachers been known at the time applications were
being approved for funding; and
   WHEREAS, Eligibility in the 1968-1969 fiscal year would have
placed such districts in a first priority position for the 1969-
1970 fiscal year as participating districts under the provisions
of Section 5792 of the Education Code; and
   WHEREAS, First priority position for the 1969-1970 fiscal
year is being denied these districts through unforeseen factors
over which the school district or the Department of Education
had no control; now, therefore, be it
   Resolved by the Senate of the State of California, the As-
sembly thereof concurring, That the members request the De-
partment of Education to include as participating districts
under the provisions of Section 5792 of the Education Code
for the 1969-1970 fiscal year, those districts which would have
received allocations for specialist teachers in reading had the
full appropriation of sixteen million dollars ($16,000,000) been
allocated for the 1968-1969 fiscal year; and be it further
   Resolved, That the Secretary of the Senate transmit a copy
of this resolution to the Superintendent of Public Instruction.

               EESOLUTION CHAPTEE 297
       Senate Concurrent Resolution No. 151—Relative to
             Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta levees.
            [Filed with Secretary of State August 8, 1969.]

   WHEREAS, The Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta, as denned
in Section 12220 of the Water Code, has been subjected to
long periods of high flow during the first half of the 1969
calendar year; and
   WHEREAS, Much of the delta consists of lands below sea level
protected by a vast network of levee systems; and
   WHEREAS, A number of delta levees failed during the early
part of 1969, and others were threatened and seriously weak-
ened by such high flows and high tides; and
   WHEREAS, Many of the levees have been constructed by local
reclamation districts and a few have been constructed and
maintained by state and federal agencies as project levees, and
some areas are protected by both locally constructed and proj-
ect levees, necessitating high standards of maintenance on
locally constructed levees to insure the functioning of the
project levees; and
  WHEREAS, The failure of any of such levees results in severe
economic loss to the local area, the state, and the United
States; and
   WHEREAS, During times of emergency large sums of federal
and state moneys are expended to keep the various levee sys-
tems from failing and to repair levees which have failed; and
                      1969
Res. Ch. 2981                REGULAR SESSION                  3969

    WHEREAS, Many of the levees within the delta area have
 deteriorated over the years due to a variety of causes, and
 others must be periodically raised to offset settlement, and
 these levees may be subject to failure at almost any time; and
    WHEKEAS, I t has become increasingly recognized that preser-
 vation of natural beauty, shade, and wildlife habitat on the
 levees is important from a recreational and esthetic viewpoint;
 now, therefore, be it
   Resolved by the Senate of the State of California, the As-
 sembly thereof concurring, That the Department of "Water
Resources is requested to undertake a general review of the
condition of all levees within the Sacramento-San Joaquin
Delta area, with particular emphasis on those levees considered
to be substandard, and to include in such review a preliminary
evaluation of the factors and costs involved in bringing the
levees up to a safe condition and maintaining them in a safe
condition and the extent to which such improvements might
reduce the requirements of emergency expenditures; and be it
further
   Resolved, That in undertaking such review recognition be
given to those areas where growth on such levees or the berms
thereof can be permitted for esthetic purposes without en-
dangering the maintenance of safe levees; and be it further
   Resolved, That recommendations be made as to the sharing
by local, state, and federal governments of costs necessary to
bring such levees up to safe standards and for the continuous
operation and maintenance thereof, and as to a means of col-
lection of such costs; and be it further
   Resolved, That the Department of Water Resources is re-
quested to confer, in making its review, with local, federal, and
other state agencies, including the State Reclamation Board,
and flood control, recreational, and navigational interests, and
to submit a preliminary report to the Legislature not later
than February 1, 1970, containing recommendations on sur-
veys and studies that are necessary to develop a comprehensive
plan of action; and be it further
   Resolved, That the Secretary of the Senate transmit a copy
of this resolution to the Director of Water Resources.

                RESOLUTION CHAPTER 299
Senate Constitutional Amendment No. 26—A resolution to pro-
  pose to the people of the State of California an amendment
  to the Constitution of the state, by amending Section 1 of
  Article XVI thereof, relating to state indebtedness.
             [Filed with Secretary of State August 8, 1969.]

   Resolved by the Senate, the Assembly concurring, That the
Legislature of the State of California at its 1969 Regular Ses-
sion commencing on the sixth day of January, 1969, two-thirds
of the members elected to each of the two houses of the Legis-
lature voting therefor, hereby proposes to the people of the
State of California that the Constitution of the state be
amended by amending Section 1 of Article X V I thereof to
read:
   SECTION 1. The Legislature shall not, in any manner create
any debt or debts, liability or liabilities, which shall, singly or
                    1969
Kes. Ch. 299]              REGULAR SESSIOK                  3971
in the aggregate with any previous debts or liabilities, exceed
the sum of three hundred thousand dollars ($300,000), except
in case of war to repel invasion or suppress insurrection, un-
less the same shall be authorized by law for some single object
or work to be distinctly specified therein which law shall pro-
vide ways and means, exclusive of loans, for the payment of
the interest of such debt or liability as it falls due, and also
to pay and discharge the principal of such debt or liability
within 50 years of the time of the contracting thereof, and
shall be irrepealable until the principal and interest thereon
shall be paid and discharged, and such law may make provision
for a sinking fund to pay the principal of such debt or liability
to commence at a time after the incurring of such debt or lia-
bility of not more than a period of one-fourth of the time of
maturity of such debt or liability; but no such law shall take
effect unless it has been passed by a two-thirds vote of all the
members elected to each house of the Legislature and until, at
a general election or at a direct primary, it shall have been
submitted to the people and shall have received a majority of
all the votes cast for and against it at such election; and all
moneys raised by authority of such law shall be applied only
to the specific object therein stated or to the payment of the
debt thereby created. Full publicity as to matters to be voted
upon by the people is afforded by the setting out of the com-
plete text of the proposed laws, together with the arguments
for and against them, in the ballot pamphlet mailed to each
elector preceding the election at which they are submitted, and
the only requirement for publication of such law shall be that
it be set out at length in ballot pamphlets which the Secretary
of State shall cause to be printed. The Legislature may, at any
time after the approval of such law by the people, reduce the
amount of the indebtedness authorized by the law to an amount
not less than the amount contracted at the time of the reduc-
tion, or it may repeal the law if no debt shall have been con-
tracted in pursuance thereof.
   Notwithstanding any other provision of this Constitution,
Members of the Legislature who are required to meet with the
State Allocation Board shall have equal rights and duties with
the nonlegislative members to vote and act upon matters pend-
ing or coming before such board for the allocation and appor-
tionment of funds to school districts for school construction
purposes or purposes related thereto.
   Notwithstanding any other provision of this constitution, or
of any bond act to the contrary, if any general obligation
bonds of the state heretofore or hereafter authorized by vote
of the people have been offered for sale and not sold, the Legis-
lature may raise the maximum rate of interest payable on all
general obligation bonds authorized but not sold, whether or
not such bonds have been offered for sale, by a statute passed
by a two-thirds vote of all members elected to each house
thereof.
3972               STATUTES OB- CALIFORNIA                [ R e s . C n . 300

   The provisions of Senate Bill No. 763 of the 1969 Regular
Session, which authorize an increase of the state general obli-
gation bond maximum interest rate from 5 percent to an
amount not in excess of 7 percent and eliminate the maximum
rate of interest payable on notes given in anticipation of the
sale of such bonds, are hereby ratified.


               RESOLUTION CHAPTER 300
Senate Concurrent Resolution No. 55—Relative to the Univer-
      sity of California and the California State Colleges.
            [Piled with Secretary of State August 8, 1969.]

   Resolved by the Senate of the State of California, the As-
sembly thereof concurring, That the Legislature requests the
University of California and the California State Colleges, in
accepting applicants for enrollment, to utilize the following
priorities:
   (1) Applicants from the public junior colleges who have
successfully completed two academic years, 50 or more semester
units, of junior college work devoted primarily to courses of
study for which transfer credit is afforded by the California
State Colleges or the University of California.
   (2) Honorably discharged veterans of United States mili-
tary service who were residents of California at the time of
their induction into the military service and who are other-
wise eligible for admission. Such priority shall be granted only
with respect to the first such application which is made by
such persons, and in no case may more than 15 percent of
the students at a state college or university campus be given
priority pursuant to this provision.
   (3) Applicants who hold a certification document issued
by the State Board of Education upon partial fulfillment of
requirements, and applicants who hold an internship creden-
tial or provisional credential issued by the State Board of
Education. Such applicants, when otherwise qualified, shall be
admitted by the state colleges to late afternoon, evening, and
summer school classes when they are required to complete State
Board of Education requirements for a partial, provisionsal or
internship credential; and be it further
  Resolved, That the Secretary of the Senate transmit copies
of this resolution to the Regents of the University of Califor-
nia and the Trustees of the California State Colleges.

 the Marine Mineral Technology Center of the Bureau of Mines
in Tiburon, California, is being reduced to the extent that the
center will be required to dismiss 35 to 45 employees and to
suspend operation of the research vessel "Virginia C i t y " ;
and
   WHEREAS, The Marine Mineral Technology Center of the
Bureau of Mines is concerned with the vital development of
unknown mineral resources of the ocean waters along the
Pacific Coast and is a function necessary for the entire United
States because, with the constant Soviet operations along the
Pacific Coast to determine the extent and possibilities of min-
eral and fishing wealth, it is imperative that our country be
the first to obtain such knowledge; and
 3976              STATUTES OF CALIFORNIA                 [EeS. Ch. 305

    WHEREAS, Curtailment of budget funds for the center would
 eliminate its offshore operations and limit accomplishments in
 the marine mineral field by the center; and
    WHEREAS, The Marine Mineral Technology Center urgently
 requires reinstatement of approximately $600,000 to its work-
 ing capital to continue the well-established work in the marine
mining program on the Continental Shelf; now, therefore,
be it
    Resolved by the Senate and Assembly of the State of Cali-
fornia, jointly, That the Legislature of the State of California
respectfully memorializes the President and the Congress of
the United States to give prompt and full approval to the
budget requirements of the Marine Mineral Technology Center
in Tiburon, California, so that its invaluable services in behalf
of the national interest may be sustained and implemented;
and be it further
   Resolved, That the Secretary of the Senate transmit copies
of this resolution to the President and Vice President of the
United States, to the Speaker of the House of Representatives,
and to each Senator and Eepresentative from California in
the Congress of the United States.
